summary: H.R. 7866, titled the 'American Lending Fairness Act of 2026', adjusts federal rules regarding interest rate exportation parity for state-chartered banks and credit unions. It allows individual states to opt out of federal preemption specifically for loans made by institutions chartered within their own state, and repeals an older section of the Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act of 1980.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to state-level opt-outs regarding federal interest rate preemption if their home state chooses to pass such a law.
affected_groups.group: State-chartered financial institutions and credit unions

affected_groups.effect: May be subject to different state-level interest rate rules for loans originated by institutions chartered in their home state.

key_provisions: Allows a state to pass a law or certify a voter decision explicitly stating it does not want federal interest rate preemption to apply to loans made by its own state-chartered insured depository institutions.
Allows a state to opt out similarly with respect to loans made by its own state-chartered insured credit unions.
Repeals Section 525 of the Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act of 1980.
Applies the new amendments to govern the legal effect of any prior state law or certification made under the repealed section of the 1980 law.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 7866, titled the 'American Lending Fairness Act of 2026', adjusts federal rules regarding interest rate exportation parity for state-chartered banks and credit unions. It allows individual states to opt out of federal preemption specifically for loans made by institutions chartered within their own state, and repeals an older section of the Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act of 1980.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes how federal interest rate exportation rules apply to state-chartered institutions by empowering individual states to opt out of preemption for their own domestic lenders, while repealing prior statutory language on the matter.
